text:
Multiple Chattanooga Mocs basketball alumni sign new professional contracts
I. B. Rains
Several former Chattanooga Mocs men's basketball players have secured new professional opportunities, according to an Aug. 19 announcement from the university. The transactions come as the summer offseason continues for many leagues.
Malachi Smith, a 2022 graduate, signed a two-way contract with the Toronto Raptors of the National Basketball Association on August 17. Smith made his NBA debut last season with the Brooklyn Nets, appearing in 15 games and starting four times while averaging 8.3 points, 3.4 rebounds, and 3.3 assists per game.
Jake Stephens, who graduated in 2023, was named to the NBA G League United Team on August 10 after competing with the Phoenix Suns in summer league play in July. The G League United team is scheduled to travel to Shanghai for exhibition games on August 28 and 30 before participating in the FIBA Intercontinental Cup from September 22-27 in Beijing.
David Jean-Baptiste signed with AEO Proteas Voulas of Greece's Elite League Second Tier on August 5 after spending three seasons with Team FOG Naestved of Denmark's BasketLigaen, where he averaged 11.7 points, 2.7 rebounds, and 2.5 assists over his most recent season.
Frank Champion signed a two-year contract with MLP Academics Heidelberg of Germany’s ProA First Division on July 24 following his recognition as Star Player of the Year for Finland’s Korisliiga during his first professional season at Korihait.
Other Chattanooga alumni currently active professionally include Jikari Johnson (Poland), Trey Bonham (Czech Republic), Tyler Millin (Slovakia), Jan Zidek (Spain), Avery Diggs (Argentina), Silvio de Sousa (Greece), Stefan Kenic (Azerbaijan), Mark Tikhonenko (Spain), Matt Ryan (Italy), Ramon Vila (Spain), Thomas Smallwood (Spain), and Kevin Bridgewaters (USA).
